regex_help.body_name_replacement:
NAME-SWAPPIN' REGEX HELP
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

This here app uses Go's regexp package, which runs on RE2 syntax.
RE2 promises linear-time matchin' and handles UTF-8 just fine.

For interactive testin' and a syntax reference, mosey on over to regex101.com
or some other regex tool (pick "Golang" as the flavor when y'all test patterns).


ANCHORS
  ^  Matches start of a name     $  Matches end of a name
  Example: ^IAM matches "IAM Servers"  |  Prod$ matches "Web-Prod"


CAPTURE GROUPS
  (.*)   Grabs any characters (greedy, takes all it can)
  (.+?)   Grabs any characters (lazy, takes the least)
  $1, $2  Use them captured bits in your replacement


EXAMPLES (one rule at a time)
  Pattern: ^IAM (.*)     Replacement: MyOrg $1
  Source: "IAM Servers"   → Result: "MyOrg Servers"

  Pattern: ^Corp-(.*)$   Replacement: MyOrg-$1
  Source: "Corp-Prod"    → Result: "MyOrg-Prod"

  Pattern: ^(DEV|QA)-    Replacement: Staging-
  Source: "DEV-Server1"   → Result: "Staging-Server1"


MULTIPLE RULES (chained up)
  Rules run in order: what rule 1 spits out, rule 2 takes in, and so on.

  Rule 1: Pattern: ^IAM (.*)     Replacement: MyOrg $1
  Rule 2: Pattern: (.*) extended  Replacement: $1 detail

  Source: "IAM Servers extended"
  After rule 1: "MyOrg Servers extended"
  After rule 2: "MyOrg Servers detail"

  Y'all can mix chained rules (like swappin' a prefix) with unrelated ones
  (like swappin' a suffix) in the same list.


CASE INSENSITIVITY
  Stick (?i) at the front of yer pattern to ignore upper/lower case:

  Pattern: (?i)^iam (.*)   Replacement: MyOrg $1
  Matches: "IAM Servers", "iam servers", "IAm Servers" → "MyOrg Servers"


TIPS
  • Rules run in order; rule 1's output is rule 2's input
  • Escape special chars: . * + [ ] ( ) | etc. with a backslash
  • If the pattern don't match nothin', the name stays put
  • Test yer patterns 'fore migration—a busted regex blocks the start
regex_help.body_browse_filter:
BROWSE & SELECT REGEX FILTER HELP
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

When the "Regex" checkbox is switched on in Browse & Select, the search box
uses Go's regexp package (RE2 syntax) to match the visible row text (for
Sensors and Packages, that includes content set / last-saved text and the object name).

With Regex OFF, search is a plain case-insensitive substring match on that same combined text.
With Regex ON, fire up full patterns for precise matchin'.


COMMON EXAMPLES
  IAM
    Matches any item with "IAM" in it

  ^IAM Asset.*
    Matches names that start with "IAM Asset"

  (?i)^iam a[ip]
    Case-insensitive start match; catches "IAM A..." where the next letter is i or p

  (Cloud|AWS).*
    Matches either Cloud... or AWS...


ANCHORS
  ^   Start of name
  $   End of name

CASE INSENSITIVITY
  Slap (?i) at the front of yer pattern, for example:
    (?i)^iam

INVALID PATTERNS
  If a regex is broken, the dialog hollers an inline "Invalid regex" message.
  No items get matched 'til the pattern is fixed up.

TIPS
  • Select All only grabs items matching the CURRENT filter
  • Deselect matchin' clears selection just for the current filter (visible rows)
  • Deselect All wipes the whole selection (every item), even hidden rows
  • Sensors/Packages lists: second column favors content set (like Content: Tanium Standard); if missin', shows "Last saved:" user (not the original author; Component Updater touches a heap of objects)
  • Escape them special characters when y'need to: \. \* \+ \[ \] \( \)
  • Use regex101 with Golang flavor for a quick test run

Ain't no system keychain reachable on this here host ({{os}}). The {{side}} API token for {{url}} can either:

  B) Get parked in plaintext in the app prefs file under your user's app data folder. Anyone (or anythin') runnin' as you on this host can read it.

companion.body_text:
Well butter my biscuits, look who clicked the About button!

Howdy there, friend!

You’ve done gone and opened the About window of this here application.

Are you my cousin? 'Cause you look mighty familiar.

This fine piece o’ software was hammered together by a good ol’ country fella who believes in strong coffee, sturdy code, and fixin’ things with duct tape when all else fails.

Thanks for stoppin’ by—now go on and enjoy the app before the chickens get out again.
